memory_verse.label: Bible Reference

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There was a special category of dedication, stronger than an ordinary vow.
When something was "devoted" to the Lord in this fullest sense, it could
not be sold or bought back. It was most holy — permanently and completely
set apart for God, with no possibility of reversal.

Not everything falls into this category, but some things do. Some
surrenders are meant to be total and final, with no clause for taking them
back.

Dear reader, this raises a searching question for our own devotion. Is
there anything in our lives that we have set apart for God in this fullest
sense — completely, irreversibly His? Or do we keep everything on a
provisional basis, ready to reclaim it if the cost becomes too high?

The early martyrs understood this. So did the missionaries who left home
knowing they would never return. Jim Elliot, before he was killed
carrying the gospel, wrote that a person is no fool who gives what he
cannot keep to gain what he cannot lose.

Jesus told a parable of a man who found treasure in a field and, in his
joy, sold everything he had to buy that field (Matt 13:44). That is the
spirit of full devotion — not grudging loss, but joyful, whole-hearted
giving because what is gained is worth infinitely more.

Paul could say, I consider everything a loss because of the surpassing
worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord (Phil 3:8).

What might God be inviting you to devote to Him fully, holding nothing
back?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there anything I have set apart for God completely and
   irreversibly?
2. Do I hold my devotion on a provisional basis, ready to reclaim it?
3. What might God be inviting me to give Him wholeheartedly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, teach me a devotion that holds nothing back. Show me what You are
calling me to give You fully, and give me joy in the surrender rather than
regret. Amen.
